title: Slim-Llama: A 4.69mW Large-Language-Model Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model
problem: LLM ASICs achieve low energy for small models (336-708M parameters) but cannot scale to billion-parameter models due to excessive external memory access (EMA) energy, requiring 26-222pJ/param.
motivation: Billion-parameter LLMs like Llama require dramatically lower energy-per-parameter to run on resource-constrained systems; extreme quantization (binary/ternary weights) combined with hardware optimizations is necessary.
method: Slim-Llama adopts binary or ternary weight quantization with new hardware optimizations for token processing, achieving 9pJ/param energy consumption and sub-5mW power for billion-parameter Llama inference.
key_novelty: Binary/ternary weight quantization combined with hardware-software codesign to achieve 9pJ/param for billion-parameter LLM inference.
contributions: Binary/ternary weight quantization enabling billion-parameter Llama
Sub-5mW power consumption for billion-param LLM
limitations: Abstract-only; accuracy impact of binary/ternary quantization, token throughput, memory bandwidth, and latency not discussed.
primary_theme: Binary-quantized LLM processor for ultra-low-power inference
